gauntlet: gate=gatekeep-pr/final recommended=1

This PR adds an Export CSV button to the reports page that downloads the whole table, paging at 100 rows with a 4-second deadline; you are its author. It delivers the button, every table column in the export, and finishing under 5 seconds through that tested paging limit, while emailed exports and audit log entries are deferred to acme/widgets#46 as the spec says.

Nothing blocks merging: the test check passed in CI on the commit being reviewed, and the description's claim that it adds tests for the CSV handler matches the code. One smaller point does not block merging: the export pages through rows with its own loop instead of the shared paging helper (src/api/export.ts:31), and fix nits can take it. After merge, the PR asks the person merging to publish the guide and the spec asks them to tag the release; the repository documents a command for each, and both are offered once the merge lands. You cannot approve your own PR.

I recommend merge because nothing blocks it and the checks passed.

Pick one:
1. merge - squash-merge the PR into main with a commit message composed from the spec. [recommended]
2. fix nits - switch the export to the shared paging helper, push, and watch the checks again.
3. stop - leave the PR open and the worktree as it is.

Type a number; show evidence prints the full record.

---

**Pick: 1 (merge)**

Freshness reads before the write:

```
gh pr view 210 -R acme/widgets --json headRefOid,state,mergeable,mergeStateStatus,body,baseRefName
gh api graphql -f query='query($o:String!,$r:String!,$n:Int!){ repository(owner:$o,name:$r){ viewerPermission pullRequest(number:$n){ viewerCanUpdateBranch viewerCanMergeAsAdmin viewerCanClose headRefOid body baseRefName } } }' -f o=acme -f r=widgets -F n=210
gh api repos/acme/widgets --jq '{allow_squash_merge,allow_merge_commit,allow_rebase_merge,squash_merge_commit_message}'
gh api repos/acme/widgets/pulls/210/comments --paginate
gh api repos/acme/widgets/issues/210/comments --paginate
gh api repos/acme/widgets/pulls/210/reviews --paginate
```

The head, body and base were unchanged. The merge state was CLEAN, squash merge was allowed, and there were no new comments.

Merge. The state is not BLOCKED, so `ADMIN_ARGS` stays empty:

```
PR_NUMBER=210
BASE_REPO=acme/widgets
ASSESSED_SHA=<assessed headRefOid>
ADMIN_ARGS=()
LANDED_SUBJECT="Add on-demand CSV export for reports"
LANDED_BODY=$(mktemp "$RUN_DIR/landed-body.XXXXXX")
cat > "$LANDED_BODY" <<'EOF'
Readers can download a report's table as CSV from the reports page. The
export carries every table column in table order with a header row, pages
at 100 rows with a 4-second deadline, and returns 404 for unknown reports.
Emailed exports and audit events follow in #46.

Refs #45
EOF
gh pr merge "$PR_NUMBER" -R "$BASE_REPO" --match-head-commit "$ASSESSED_SHA" --squash --subject "$LANDED_SUBJECT (#$PR_NUMBER)" --body-file - "${ADMIN_ARGS[@]}" < "$LANDED_BODY"
gh pr view 210 -R acme/widgets --json state,mergeCommit
```

The result was MERGED with merge commit 9f1c2d3e4b5a6978, so `pr.state` and `pr.merge_commit` were recorded. The coverage block was saved as `$RUN_DIR/coverage-ticket.md` and `$RUN_DIR/coverage-pr.md` with these identical contents:

## AC coverage
Informational - the ticket's rows are unchanged. PR https://github.com/acme/widgets/pull/210, merged 9f1c2d3e4b5a6978, spec doc/specs/2026-09-30-csv-export.md
- [ ] AC1 The reports page offers an Export CSV button. - covered
- [ ] AC2 The export includes every column shown in the table. - covered
- [ ] AC3 Exports are emailed to the requesting user. - deferred per spec to acme/widgets#46
- [ ] AC4 The export completes under 5s on production data. - covered
- [ ] AC5 Export events appear in the audit log. - deferred per spec to acme/widgets#46
